title: NASA’s New Space Telescope Begins Its Journey to Uncover Cosmic Mysteries
subtitle: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has successfully launched, marking a new era in our exploration of the universe.

summary.en: NASA has successfully launched the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope from Florida. The powerful new observatory is now on a journey to a location one million miles from Earth. It is designed to study dark energy, dark matter, and thousands of distant planets. This mission is the first NASA telescope named after a female scientist. Scientists expect the telescope to provide a much wider view of the universe than previous missions.
summary.zh: 美國國家航空暨太空總署已成功從佛羅里達州發射南希·葛瑞絲·羅曼太空望遠鏡。這台強大的新觀測站目前正前往距離地球一百萬英里的位置。其設計目的是研究暗能量、暗物質以及數千顆遙遠的行星。這是美國國家航空暨太空總署首個以女性科學家命名的太空望遠鏡。科學家預期該望遠鏡將比過往任務提供更廣闊的宇宙視野。

paragraphs.en: NASA has successfully launched its newest and most powerful space telescope, the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. The spacecraft took off on Sunday morning from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida, carried by a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket. According to BBC News, the launch was a major success, with project manager Jackie Townsend describing the ride as "magnificent" and noting that the telescope is now exactly where it needs to be to begin its mission.
paragraphs.zh: 美國國家航空暨太空總署（NASA）已成功發射其最新且最強大的太空望遠鏡——南希·葛瑞絲·羅曼太空望遠鏡（Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope）。該太空船於週日上午從佛羅里達州的甘迺迪太空中心（Kennedy Space Center）升空，由太空探索科技公司（SpaceX）的獵鷹重型運載火箭（Falcon Heavy）搭載。根據英國廣播公司新聞（BBC News）報導，此次發射取得重大成功，計畫經理潔姬·湯森（Jackie Townsend）形容升空過程「極其壯觀」，並指出望遠鏡目前已抵達執行任務所需的精確位置。

paragraphs.en: This mission is a significant step forward for space exploration. As reported by NPR News, the telescope is about the size of a tour bus and weighs 18,000 pounds. It is currently traveling toward a specific point in space called L2, which is roughly one million miles away from Earth. This location is the same spot where the James Webb Space Telescope operates. By staying at this distance, the telescope can avoid interference from the heat and light of the Earth and the Moon, allowing its sensitive cameras to work clearly.
paragraphs.zh: 這項任務是太空探索的一大躍進。據美國公共廣播電台（NPR News）報導，這台望遠鏡的大小約與遊覽車相當，重量達一萬八千磅。它目前正前往距離地球約一百萬英里的太空特定點，稱為「拉格朗日點二號」（L2）。該位置與詹姆斯·韋伯太空望遠鏡（James Webb Space Telescope）的運作位置相同。透過保持在此距離，望遠鏡能避開來自地球與月球的熱能及光線干擾，讓其靈敏的攝影機得以清晰運作。

paragraphs.en: The telescope is named after Nancy Grace Roman, who was NASA’s first chief astronomer in the 1960s. She is often called the "Mother of Hubble" because of her important work in getting the Hubble Space Telescope approved. According to DW, this is the first time NASA has named a space telescope after a woman. Retired scientist Ed Weiler noted that this honor was long overdue and that Nancy Grace Roman would likely be very proud of the project.
paragraphs.zh: 這台望遠鏡以南希·葛瑞絲·羅曼（Nancy Grace Roman）命名，她是美國國家航空暨太空總署在一九六零年代的首位首席天文學家。由於她在推動哈伯太空望遠鏡（Hubble Space Telescope）立項過程中的重要貢獻，她常被稱為「哈伯之母」。根據德國之聲（DW）報導，這是美國國家航空暨太空總署首次以女性名字為太空望遠鏡命名。已退休的科學家艾德·威勒（Ed Weiler）表示，這項榮譽遲到了許久，南希·葛瑞絲·羅曼若在世，想必會對此計畫感到非常驕傲。

paragraphs.en: One of the main goals of the mission is to solve deep mysteries about how the universe works. Scientists want to learn more about dark energy and dark matter. Dark matter is an invisible substance that acts like a type of "gravitational glue" to hold galaxies together. Dark energy, on the other hand, is a mysterious force that scientists believe is pushing the universe to expand. Together, these two invisible things are thought to make up about 95% of the universe. By studying these forces, researchers hope to understand the past and future of the cosmos.
paragraphs.zh: 該任務的主要目標之一是解開關於宇宙運作方式的深奧謎團。科學家希望深入了解暗能量與暗物質。暗物質是一種無形的物質，作用如同某種「重力膠水」，將星系凝聚在一起。另一方面，暗能量則是一種神祕的力量，科學家認為正是它在推動宇宙膨脹。這兩者被認為共同構成了宇宙約百分之九十五的成分。透過研究這些力量，研究人員希望能理解宇宙的過去與未來。

paragraphs.en: Beyond these dark forces, the telescope will also search for exoplanets, which are planets located outside of our own solar system. NASA administrator Nicky Fox stated that the telescope could discover tens of thousands, or perhaps even 100,000, new planets. The primary goal of this search is to help answer the fundamental question: "Are we alone in the universe?" The telescope will also map billions of galaxies and study black holes with a level of detail that has never been possible before.
paragraphs.zh: 除了這些暗黑力量，該望遠鏡也將搜尋太陽系外的系外行星。美國國家航空暨太空總署署長妮基·福克斯（Nicky Fox）表示，這台望遠鏡可能發現數萬甚至十萬顆新行星。這項搜尋的主要目標是協助回答一個根本性的問題：「我們在宇宙中是孤獨的嗎？」該望遠鏡也將繪製數十億個星系的圖譜，並以史無前例的細節研究黑洞。

paragraphs.en: What makes this telescope special is its massive field of view. According to DW, the Roman telescope can see an area of space 100 times larger than what the Hubble or James Webb telescopes can see at one time. This means it can survey the sky much faster. In fact, scientists estimate that the Roman telescope can complete observations in one month that would have taken the Hubble telescope an entire century to finish. This efficiency is expected to generate over 500 terabytes of data every year, providing a massive amount of information for astronomers to study.
paragraphs.zh: 這台望遠鏡的特殊之處在於其巨大的視野。根據德國之聲報導，羅曼太空望遠鏡一次能觀測的太空區域，是哈伯或詹姆斯·韋伯太空望遠鏡的一百倍。這意味著它能以快得多的速度進行巡天觀測。事實上，科學家估計羅曼太空望遠鏡在一個月內完成的觀測量，哈伯太空望遠鏡需要整整一個世紀才能完成。預計這種高效率每年將產生超過五百兆位元組的數據，為天文學家提供海量的研究資訊。

paragraphs.en: The journey to its final destination will take about three months. During this time, ground controllers at NASA will be busy checking all the systems to ensure everything is working perfectly. Jeremy Perkins, a scientist on the mission, explained that this is a time to "kick the tires" and make sure the focus and pointing of the telescope are exactly right. Once these tests are finished, the telescope will begin its primary mission, which is expected to last for five years, with a goal of operating for up to 10 years.
paragraphs.zh: 前往最終目的地的旅程將耗時約三個月。在此期間，美國國家航空暨太空總署的地面控制人員將忙於檢查所有系統，確保一切運作完美。任務科學家傑瑞米·柏金斯（Jeremy Perkins）解釋道，這段時間是用來進行「壓力測試」，確保望遠鏡的對焦與指向完全精準。一旦這些測試完成，望遠鏡將展開預計為期五年的主要任務，並以運作長達十年為目標。

paragraphs.en: This project has been a long time in the making. Interestingly, the telescope has an unusual history; it was originally designed as a spy telescope for the National Reconnaissance Office before being donated to NASA. With a budget of over $4 billion, the mission represents a massive investment in our understanding of space. The first images from the telescope are expected to reach Earth in early 2027. As the telescope continues its journey, scientists around the world are waiting with excitement to see what new secrets it will reveal about the vast, mysterious universe we live in.
paragraphs.zh: 這個計畫醞釀已久。有趣的是，這台望遠鏡有一段不尋常的歷史；它最初是為國家偵察局（National Reconnaissance Office）設計的間諜望遠鏡，後來才捐贈給美國國家航空暨太空總署。該任務預算超過四十億美元，代表著對我們理解太空的一項巨大投資。預計望遠鏡傳回的第一批影像將於二零二七年初抵達地球。隨著望遠鏡繼續其旅程，全球科學家正興奮地等待它揭開我們所處這片廣闊且神祕宇宙的全新祕密。

keyTerms.definitionEn: Something that should have happened a long time ago.
keyTerms.noteZh: 此片語常用於表達某事延遲已久。文中：Retired scientist Ed Weiler noted that this honor was long overdue and that Nancy Grace Roman would likely be very proud of the project.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To perform a final check or test on something to ensure it is working correctly before it is put into full use.
keyTerms.definitionZh: （在正式使用前）進行最後的檢查或測試。
keyTerms.noteZh: 字面意思是「踢輪胎」，但在這裡指對設備進行檢查。文中：Jeremy Perkins, a scientist on the mission, explained that this is a time to "kick the tires" and make sure the focus and pointing of the telescope are exactly right.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Being created or developed over a long period of time.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常用來形容一項計畫經歷了很長的準備期。文中：This project has been a long time in the making.

previousArticles.summaryEn: NASA has successfully launched the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope from Florida. The telescope will travel one million miles to reach a special location in space called L2. It is designed to study mysterious forces like dark energy and dark matter. The project was named after Nancy Grace Roman, a famous astronomer who helped create the Hubble Space Telescope. Scientists hope this mission will help us understand how the universe grows and changes.

quiz.question: What is the primary reason the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is positioned at the L2 point?

options.A: To be closer to the James Webb Space Telescope for maintenance.
options.B: To minimize interference from the heat and light of Earth and the Moon.
options.C: To allow the telescope to travel faster toward the edge of the universe.
options.D: To avoid the gravitational pull of the SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第二段，該望遠鏡位於 L2 點是為了避開地球與月球的熱源與光線干擾，確保感應相機運作清晰。A 選項雖提到與 James Webb 在同一位置，但並非為了維修；C 選項文章未提及此位置能增加速度；D 選項則無關，火箭僅負責發射。

quiz.question: Based on the information provided, what can be inferred about the Roman telescope's efficiency compared to its predecessors?

options.A: It is designed specifically to replace the Hubble telescope within one year.
options.B: It will require significantly more human labor to process its data than previous telescopes.
options.C: It is capable of surveying larger areas of the sky in a much shorter timeframe.
options.D: It is less sensitive to dark matter than the James Webb Space Telescope.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第六段，該望遠鏡的視野是 Hubble 或 James Webb 的 100 倍，且一個月內完成的觀測量相當於 Hubble 一個世紀的工作量，故可推論其觀測效率極高。A 選項文章未提及取代計畫；B 選項未提及人力需求；D 選項文章並未比較兩者對暗物質的敏感度。

quiz.question: In the seventh paragraph, what does the phrase 'kick the tires' mean in the context of the mission?

options.A: To perform a physical inspection of the telescope's exterior.
options.B: To test and verify that all systems are functioning correctly.
options.C: To forcefully push the telescope into its final orbit.
options.D: To prepare the telescope for its first encounter with a black hole.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。此慣用語原指買車前檢查輪胎狀況，在文中被引申為在正式任務開始前，進行徹底的系統檢查與測試，確保一切運作正常。A 選項過於字面解讀；C 選項與物理推動無關；D 選項則是對任務目標的錯誤解讀。

quiz.question: What is the central purpose of the Roman Space Telescope mission?

options.A: To serve as a replacement for the National Reconnaissance Office's spy satellites.
options.B: To honor Nancy Grace Roman by naming a NASA project after her for the first time.
options.C: To exclusively focus on mapping the surface of planets outside our solar system.
options.D: To advance our understanding of the universe through studying dark forces and searching for new planets.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 D。綜合文章第四、五段，該任務的核心目標是研究暗能量與暗物質，並搜尋太陽系外的行星以探討生命起源，這是任務的主要科學目的。A 選項僅是歷史背景；B 選項是命名由來，非任務目的；C 選項太過狹隘，忽略了對暗物質與星系的研究。
